app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.
info.title: Crawlora API

get.description: Returns the complete filter taxonomy for the Creative Center trend endpoints: the countries each trend tab reports, the industry ids and video content tags the filters accept, the supported lookback periods, and the video sort metrics. Use it to discover valid values for the hashtags endpoint's country_code, period, and industry_id parameters and the videos endpoint's country_code, period, sort_by, and content_label_ids parameters. get.description: Returns TikTok Creative Center's ranked trending hashtags for a country, period, and optional industry. TikTok gates this endpoint's full result set behind a logged-in TikTok One account: an anonymous request always receives at most 3 hashtags per filter combination regardless of country, period, or industry, so selecting an industry returns that industry's own ranked top three. See the filters endpoint for the complete country, period, and industry value lists.

get.description: Returns TikTok Creative Center's current Top Content set: four top-performing branded videos, each with the video object (anonymous MP4 and cover URLs), engagement metrics, the author profile and follower count, and (by default) the video's top comments plus keyword mention counts derived from them. The set is a daily snapshot and there is no pagination or historical query; the four titles rotate when the snapshot changes. Set include_comments=false for a smaller response with only video, author, and metrics.

get.description: Returns TikTok Creative Center's ranked trending videos for a country, period, sort order, and optional content tags. TikTok reports the true result-set size (see total_count/page_count in the response) but gates access to it behind a logged-in TikTok One account: an anonymous request always receives page 1 (4 videos) regardless of sort order or period. Country coverage is uneven: only US, JP, ID, VN, and TH have a regional edge host that returns populated results; other countries return an empty videos array (a genuine no-data response, not an error). See the filters endpoint for the complete country, period, sort, and content tag value lists.

get.description: Calls the app's cached-pull feed route - `GET /tiktok/feed/offline/v2` - which answers protobuf, and returns a schema-free decode: field numbers become keys, printable length-delimited fields become strings and nested messages become objects, plus a flat list of every string leaf (`strings`), which is the fastest way to mine video ids and captions. Field numbering is inferred because TikTok publishes no schema for this message. This is the cached/offline pull variant, not the primary `POST /aweme/v2/feed/` feed already exposed as `/tiktok/mobile/feed/post`.

parameters.description: Pull type forwarded to the app route (measured 0 and 11; default 11)
parameters.name: pull_type

parameters.description: Page size, bounded at 50 (upstream default when omitted)
parameters.name: count

get.description: Calls the app's primary feed route - `POST /aweme/v2/feed/`, which the Android client sends with a protobuf request body and answers with protobuf - and returns a schema-free decode: field numbers become keys, length-delimited fields become strings when printable, nested messages when they parse and base64 otherwise, plus a flat list of every string leaf. Field numbering is inferred because TikTok publishes no schema for this message; use the JSON `GET /tiktok/mobile/feed` route when you need the stable structured contract.
get.summary: Fetch the app's primary feed call (POST, protobuf) decoded without a schema

get.description: Returns the reference set the app's "go LIVE" flow uses to tag a stream: the general LIVE hashtags (`hashtags`, measured 18 entries of `{id, image, namespace, title}`, where `id` 0 is the "None" tag), the live-studio/live-voice/third-party hashtag subsets (`live_studio_hashtags` 16, `live_voice_hashtags` 16, `third_party_hashtags` 9), the single `game_hashtag`, and a 1,500-entry game catalogue (`game_tag_list`, `game_tag_count`) where every entry carries the same 12 keys: `id`, `short_name`, `show_name`, `full_name`, `bundle_id`, `package_name`, `game_category` (`[{game_type, title}]` with PC games/Mobile games/Console games/Others), `hashtag_id`, `hashtag_list`, `gar`, `landscape` (0/1/2) and `is_new_game`. The upstream is `/webcast/room/hashtag/list/` on the webcast edge host (no origin header); the measured body is 539,361 B and byte-identical on both working webcast hosts, `language`/`count` do not change it, and there is no cursor/has_more, so it is a one-shot reference dump. get.description: Returns one LIVE room's detail, keyed by `room_id` — the numeric id that `/api/v1/tiktok/mobile/live/search` returns under `data[].lives.author.room_id`. The upstream is `/webcast/room/info/` on the webcast edge host (no origin header), captured from the running 47.4.3 app's LIVE surface and reproduced against the live gateway. The response projects the fields callers key on — `title`, `status` (2 = live), `user_count` (concurrent viewers), `create_time`, `owner` (user id, nickname, avatar), `stats` (cumulative `enter_count`/`total_user`, `watch_user_count`, `like_count`, `comment_count`, `share_count`, `follow_count`, `replay_viewers`), `stream` (playable `flv_pull_url` per resolution plus `default_resolution`/`candidate_resolution` and the HLS/RTMP URLs) and `cover` — and keeps the upstream room object unmodified in `data` (it has ~500 keys, so a partial struct would drop fields). Measured 2026-10-22: one room returned 193-198 KB with 1,595-1,600 concurrent viewers, 27,916 cumulative viewers, 27,096 enters and FLV URLs for FULL_HD1/HD1/SD1/SD2. `anchor_id` is deliberately NOT forwarded: it was measured to suppress the audience-only `stats.total_user` (27,916 -> 0 on the same room). A missing, non-numeric or unknown room id answers the webcast envelope's status 10011 and is surfaced as a 400; a finished room (status 30003) is a 400 too.

400.description: Invalid input, an unknown/not-live room, or a finished room

get.summary: LIVE room detail: status, viewers, owner, stream URLs, cover

get.description: Returns the LIVE room a TikTok user is currently streaming, keyed by `user_id`. The upstream is `/webcast/room/info_by_user/` on the webcast edge host (no origin header) and returns the same room payload as `/api/v1/tiktok/mobile/live/room` (title, status, concurrent viewers, owner, cumulative stats, per-resolution FLV URLs, cover and the ~500-key room object in `data`), except that the caller addresses a user and the room id is filled from the payload (both `user_id` and `room_id` are echoed). Measured 2026-10-22: `user_id=6707748031095751686` answered 184,575 B (195,220 B on the second webcast host); `anchor_id` alone answers a 57-byte empty payload, so `user_id` is the address. A user with no live room answers status 30003 "room has finished" and is surfaced as a 400; a non-numeric user id is a 400 (status 10011); a bare call answers a 57-byte empty success envelope, which is why this endpoint requires `user_id`.

get.description: Returns one video's own captions translated into the requested language, as TikTok's caption/language (`cla`) service serves them. The response carries the track twice: `webvtt` is the upstream WebVTT text verbatim, and `cues` is the same track parsed into `{start_ms, end_ms, start, end, text}` records so a caller does not have to implement WebVTT. `video_id` is the aweme id returned by the feed, search, profile-posts and hashtag endpoints. Measured 2026-10-21: the Korean-caption video 7696141388324293918 answered 11 English cues for `language=en`, and the same video answered Japanese, Chinese, Spanish, French, German, Korean, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Hindi, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Turkish and Italian tracks; a Portuguese-lyrics video answered an 18,494-character English track (240 cues). Track size is a snapshot rather than a contract (the upstream re-translates from a cache), so assert a non-empty track in the requested language, not a byte count. A video with no captions answers 400 (upstream status 5); a nonexistent video answers 500 (upstream status 4).
